_readme: Ground truth for the eval golden set. Every entry is derived from published
literature, NOT from this agent's output. Do not edit an expected value
because the agent missed it -- a miss is a result, not a labelling error.
provenance.gap_source records the granularity actually verified:
'section: <heading>'  the survey's own future-work section was retrieved
and the keywords come from the directions it names.
'abstract'            only the abstract/table of contents was retrieved;
keywords are the survey's stated scope, which is
weaker ground truth. Reported as a limitation.
'debate'              contested topic: ground truth is the pair of papers
that disagree, not a survey's future-work section.
Every arxiv_id below was verified by fetching its arXiv abstract page on
2026-08-07 and checking the title matched. Expected paper titles are stored
as lowercase-able substrings; matching is substring, case-insensitive.

cases.topic: retrieval-augmented generation versus long-context language models
cases.idea: use retrieval to pre-filter passages before a long-context model

provenance.survey_title: (contested) Retrieval meets Long Context Large Language Models vs Lost in the Middle: How Language Models Use Long Contexts
provenance.gap_note: 2310.03025 reports retrieval augmentation matching or beating a much longer context window; 2307.03172 reports degradation for information in the middle of long contexts. The RAG survey (2312.10997 section VII) names 'RAG vs Long Context' as an explicit open question.
provenance.paper_source: both sides of the disagreement; titles verified on arXiv

provenance.gap_note: 2206.07682 reports abilities appearing sharply past a scale threshold; 2304.15004 argues the sharpness is an artefact of discontinuous metrics rather than a property of the model.
provenance.paper_source: both sides of the disagreement; titles verified on arXiv

cases.topic: self-correction and self-refinement in large language model reasoning

provenance.gap_note: 2303.17651 reports gains from iterative self-feedback without extra training; 2310.01798 reports that without external feedback, self-correction degrades reasoning performance.
provenance.paper_source: both sides of the disagreement; titles verified on arXiv
